caption_hook: New York has been a glacier's dumping ground, a river delta and a mountain range older than dinosaurs.

layers.name: HARBOR HILL MORAINE
layers.what: At its farthest reach, a mile-thick ice sheet bulldozed rock, sand and boulders south and dumped them in a long ridge. That heap of debris became the backbone of Long Island.
layers.bonus: The ridge is named for Harbor Hill in Roslyn, which tops out at about 350 feet.

layers.name: CATSKILL FORMATION
layers.hook: Red mud from a vanished range
layers.what: Rivers poured sand and mud off a huge mountain range to the east and built a giant delta. The red and gray rock now forms the Catskill Mountains, cut by streams into cliffs and waterfalls.
layers.bonus: Near Gilboa, fossil tree stumps about 385 million years old are among the oldest ever found.

layers.name: LOCKPORT DOLOMITE
layers.hook: The hard cap on Niagara Falls
layers.what: A warm, shallow sea left thick beds of limestone-like dolomite. This tough layer sits on top of softer shale, and it is the reason Niagara Falls exists.
layers.bonus: Water wears away the soft rock below, so the falls have retreated about seven miles upriver.

layers.name: MANHATTAN SCHIST
layers.what: When ancient continents collided, mud and sand were buried deep, squeezed and baked into glittering, mica-rich schist. The bedrock under much of Manhattan is this tough, layered stone.
layers.bonus: Glaciers polished and grooved the schist bumps that still poke through Central Park's grass.

layers.name: POTSDAM SANDSTONE
layers.hook: A beach from the dawn of animal life
layers.what: A shallow sea washed sand onto the edges of what is now the Adirondacks. The sand hardened into red and tan sandstone, and the Ausable River has since sliced a deep chasm through it.
layers.bonus: Ausable Chasm has drawn sightseers since the 1800s and is nicknamed the Grand Canyon of the Adirondacks.

layers.name: ADIRONDACK ANORTHOSITE
layers.hook: The ancient core of the mountains
layers.what: Deep underground, molten rock cooled slowly into a pale, coarse rock called anorthosite. Mount Marcy, the state's highest point at 5,344 ft, is made of it.
layers.bonus: These mountains are still rising, by about 2 millimeters a year, even as they erode.
